extracted.intended_audience: Medicare providers, contractors, hospitals, organ procurement organizations (OPOs), and CMS/legal/administrative staff responsible for compliance with CMS rules
extracted.subtask_short: Medicare appeals and cost reimbursement rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory provisions governing contractor hearings and administrative review procedures, prospective payment/add-on payment eligibility, and principles of cost reimbursement (allowable/unallowable costs, overhead allocation, and related documentation) for Medicare providers, hospitals, and OPOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount in controversy requirement for contractor hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of an IOPO or histocompatibility laboratory, the amount in controversy (as determined in accordance with § 405.1839) must be at least $1,000 but less than $10,000. An IOPO or histocompatibility laboratory is subject to the amount in controversy requirement specified in § 413.420(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies monetary thresholds that determine eligibility for a contractor hearing; references §405.1839 for determination method and §413.420(g) for exceptions (IOPO/histocompatibility lab).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness for requesting a contractor hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the provider qualifies for a good cause extension under § 405.1813, the date of receipt by the contractor of the provider's hearing request must be no later than 180 days after the date of receipt by the provider of the final contractor or Secretary determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing requests received after 180 days are untimely absent a good cause extension; IOPO/histocompatibility labs are subject to different provisions per §413.420(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause extension: finality and reviewability
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision denying an extension request and dismissing the appeal is final and binding on the provider, unless the dismissal decision is reviewed by a CMS reviewing official, reviewed by the Administrator, or reopened and revised by the contractor hearing officer(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor hearing officer must promptly send denial decisions to the appropriate CMS component. A decision granting an extension is not subject to immediate review but may be examined during later CMS reviewing official or Administrator reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor hearing officer jurisdiction and limits on further review
rubrics_metrics.description: Final jurisdictional findings and jurisdictional dismissal decisions by the contractor hearing officer(s) are subject to the CMS reviewing official procedure and possible Administrator review; nevertheless, a contractor hearing officer's jurisdictional findings as to specific matters may be reviewed solely during the course of specified CMS reviewing official or Administrator reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that jurisdictional findings are generally final except when specifically captured within the enumerated review processes; lists the limited avenues when jurisdictional issues can be revisited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate review of discovery or disclosure rulings involving privilege/protection
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent a ruling authorizes discovery or disclosure of a matter for which an objection based on privilege or other protection from disclosure was made before the contractor hearing officer(s), that portion of the discovery or disclosure ruling may immediately be reviewed by a CMS reviewing official or the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If immediate review is sought (or own motion review suggested), the contractor hearing officer must be notified and stays all proceedings affected by the ruling pending review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of a contractor hearing decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractor hearing decision issued in accordance with § 405.1831 is final and binding on all parties to the contractor hearing and on the contractor, unless the contractor hearing decision is reviewed by a CMS reviewing official (and possibly the Administrator) or reopened and revised by the contractor hearing officer(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the baseline finality of contractor hearing decisions and the limited circumstances under which they may be altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement and scope of CMS reviewing official review
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS or a provider that is a party to, and dissatisfied with, a final decision by the contractor hearing officer(s), upon submitting a request that meets the requirements of paragraph (c), is entitled to further administrative review by a designated CMS reviewing official. The CMS reviewing official considers whether the contractor hearing officer's decision is consistent with the controlling legal authority and the evidence in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No other individual or entity has the right to the review; review is first by the designated CMS reviewing official and may be followed by discretionary Administrator review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness for submitting a request to the CMS reviewing official
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of receipt by the appropriate CMS component of the review request is no later than 60 days after the date of receipt by the provider of the contractor hearing officer decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a 60-day deadline for parties (or CMS) to request review by the CMS reviewing official; late requests will not meet the procedural requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness for immediate review of discovery/disclosure rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: A request from a party or CMS for immediate review of a contractor hearing officer ruling authorizing discovery or disclosure must be made as soon as practicable after the ruling is made, but in no event later than 5 business days after the date the requesting party or CMS received notice of the ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a very short window (5 business days) for seeking immediate review of sensitive discovery/disclosure rulings to protect privileged materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS reviewing official own-motion review discretion and administrator backstop
rubrics_metrics.description: The CMS reviewing official has discretion to take own motion review of a contractor hearing officer decision or other reviewable action. If the CMS reviewing official does not notify intent to review within 90 days after the contractor hearing officer's decision, the Administrator may issue a notice instructing the CMS reviewing official to review the decision; if the CMS reviewing official still fails to act, the Administrator may step in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides both CMS reviewing official discretion and a timeline/backstop mechanism by which the Administrator can compel or prompt review to prevent indefinite inaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents and possible outcomes of a CMS reviewing official decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of the review of a contractor hearing decision, the CMS reviewing official issues a written decision that includes findings of fact and conclusions of law on jurisdictional issues and on the merits of each issue under review and affirms, reverses, or modifies the contractor hearing decision or remands the contractor hearing decision to the contractor hearing officer for further proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision must be promptly sent to each party, to the contractor, and to the appropriate component of CMS. A remand is not a final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of a CMS reviewing official decision and remand mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision of affirmation, reversal, or modification by the CMS reviewing official is final and binding on each party and the contractor, except as provided for Administrator review or reopening. A remand must require specified actions by the entity to which the matter is remanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS reviewing official decisions may be reopened and revised under §§405.1885–405.1889; remands impose specific duties and the remand process must follow criteria similar to remands by the Administrator to the Board (§405.1875(f)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator review: discretionary authority and request content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS or any party to a CMS reviewing official decision may request Administrator review in accordance with this section; the Administrator may grant or deny review at his or her discretion. A request must be in writing, attach a copy of the CMS reviewing official decision, and include a brief description of: (A) aspects of the decision with which the requestor is dissatisfied; (B) reasons for dissatisfaction; (C) any argument or record evidence supporting its position; and (D) any additional extra-record evidence relied on, with demonstration that such evidence was improperly excluded below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for Administrator review by a party or CMS must be filed within 15 days of receipt of the CMS reviewing official decision and must be sent to the Office of the Attorney Advisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator notice and decision timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator must issue a Notice advising parties of intent to review or decline to review within 30 days of receipt of a request; the Administrator may issue a Notice of Review on own motion within 45 days of receipt of a CMS reviewing official's decision. If the Administrator does not issue timely determinations, the CMS reviewing official's decision becomes final. If the Administrator elects to review, the Administrator sets deadlines for comments and the Administrator's decision affirming, reversing, or modifying the CMS reviewing official's decision is final and binding. If the Administrator does not issue a written decision within 60 days of the Notice of Review, the CMS reviewing official's decision becomes final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies multiple timing benchmarks (30, 45, 60 days) that control when decisions become final and when Administrator action is required; includes process for notice distribution and solicitation of comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCHQR Program eCQM reporting technology requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting electronic clinical quality measures (eCQMs) under the PCHQR Program, PCHs must use: (1) Health IT certified to the ONC Health IT Certification Program criteria necessary for eCQM reporting, as adopted and updated at 45 CFR 170.315(c); (2) certified health IT to calculate, export, and submit results for the eCQMs available to report under the PCHQR Program; and (3) the eCQM electronic measure specifications for the applicable reporting period available on the eCQI Resource Center website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the technical certification and specification sources required for electronic submission of quality measures by PCHs (Prospective Payment System-Exempt Cancer Hospitals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for alternative/add-on payment pathway for certain transformative devices
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications submitted for new technology add-on payments for FYs 2021 through 2027, CMS provides for additional payments beyond standard DRG and outlier payments to a hospital for discharges involving covered inpatient hospital services that are new medical devices, if the specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule creates an alternative pathway with conditions to be satisfied for applicants seeking new technology add-on payments for transformative devices (details reside in paragraph (b) of §412.87).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for alternative pathway for certain antimicrobial products
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications submitted for new technology add-on payments for FYs 2021 through 2027, a new medical product is eligible if (1) it is designated by FDA as a Qualified Infectious Disease Product and has received marketing authorization for the indication covered by that designation; or (2) for applications submitted for FYs 2022 through 2027, it is approved under FDA's Limited Population Pathway for Antibacterial and Antifungal Drugs (LPAD) and used for the indication approved under LPAD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies FDA designation/approval pathways that make antimicrobial products eligible under the alternative add-on payment pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for FDA marketing authorization for add-on payment consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS only considers, for add-on payments for a particular fiscal year, an application for which the new medical service or technology has received FDA marketing authorization by May 1 prior to the particular fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a firm FDA authorization cutoff (May 1 prior to the FY) for consideration of add-on payment applications for that fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident enrollment and approved teaching program criteria for GME special treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The resident must be enrolled in an approved teaching program. An approved teaching program is one that: (A) is approved by one of the national organizations listed in §415.152; (B) may count towards certification of the participant in a specialty or subspecialty listed in specified directories (AMA Directory of Graduate Medical Education Programs or ABMS Annual Report and Reference Handbook); or (C) is approved by ACGME, or another organization designated by the Secretary, as a fellowship program in geriatric medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines what constitutes an 'approved teaching program' for purposes of special treatment related to indirect GME cost calculation and reimbursement; references §413.84 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence requirement for hospital redesignation proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: To demonstrate proximity to the area, the hospital must submit evidence from a nationally recognized electronic mapping service of the shortest route from the front entrance of the hospital over improved roads or waterways traveled by ferry boats to the county line of the requested area and the distance of that route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires specific mapping-source evidence and route/distance measurement methodology (shortest route over improved roads/waterways) when seeking redesignation to another rural or urban area under §412.230.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on entertainment costs as allowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by providers for entertainment, including costs associated with entertainment activities, or that are entertainment in nature, are not allowable costs. This includes items such as tickets to sporting or other events, sponsorships of sporting events/teams/athletes, sponsorship of floats in parades, concerts/theater/performers, wine tours/alcoholic beverages, retreats at spas or luxury resorts, golf outings, ski trips, cruises, and similar recreational excursions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically lists numerous examples of entertainment costs that are non-allowable; also states that this paragraph includes costs that OPOs incur to engage in public education to increase awareness of organ donation (but see separate allowability rule for OPO public education).

rubrics_metrics.name: OPO public education costs: conditional allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by OPOs to engage in public education within its donation service area to increase awareness of organ donation and increase donor registration are allowable if they are reasonable and do not violate the prohibition on entertainment costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a carve-out allowing OPO public education if reasonable and not an entertainment activity; still subject to the general entertainment prohibition in paragraph (c)(10).

rubrics_metrics.name: OPO professional education cost allowability rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by OPOs: (i) for professional education such as meetings, seminars, and presentations on organ donation to acquire all useable organs from potential donors where continuing education credits are not given and the attendee is clinical staff are allowable; (ii) for OPO-sponsored seminars where continuing education credits are given and the attendee is on OPO staff are allowable to the extent patient-care related, reasonable and necessary; and (iii) for OPO-sponsored seminars where continuing education credits are given and the attendee is not on OPO staff, such costs are not allowable in accordance with §413.402(d)(2)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes allowability based on attendee status (OPO staff vs non-staff) and whether continuing education credits are given; ties allowability to being patient-care related, reasonable and necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee travel and education cost allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by providers for employee travel are generally allowable to the extent that they are patient-care related, reasonable and necessary; travel not related to patient care is not allowable. Costs for entertainment and vacation travel (e.g., cruises, resorts, spas, transportation to entertainment/sporting events) are not allowable regardless of connection to education; costs related to personal use of provider vehicles are not allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the standard that travel must be patient-care related and reasonable/necessary to be allowable; explicitly prohibits entertainment/vacation travel and personal-use vehicle costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meals and refreshments cost non-allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred for meals sold to visitors, meals for employees and staff (including executives and management) and non-personnel are not allowable costs. Costs for meals and refreshments provided to attendees at educational events, including attendees of OPO-sponsored seminars (with or without continuing education credits), are not allowable costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad prohibition on meal-related costs as allowable Medicare cost report items, including meals provided at educational events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpatient drug sales, fines, penalties, and gift shop costs not allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by providers for drugs sold to other than patients are not related to patient care and are not allowable costs. Costs for fines or penalties resulting from Federal, State or local laws are not allowable. Costs incurred for operation of a gift shop are not allowable costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists multiple categories of business/nonpatient-related costs that must be excluded from Medicare reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudent buyer standard for patient-care costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The prudent buyer is a person, provider type or entity that purchases items or property with caution, good judgment, and a sensible approach. Providers are expected to economize by not paying more than the going price for an item or service so that their actual costs will not exceed what a prudent and cost-conscious buyer would pay. If costs exceed the level that prudent buyers incur, the excess costs are not reimbursable absent clear evidence that the higher costs were unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms an economic reasonableness standard for allowable costs and provides the benchmark 'prudent buyer' for cost comparisons and reimbursement determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on improper allocation of overhead and allowable allocation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers must not include a statistical cost which does not relate to the allocation of administrative and general expenses when it causes an improper distribution of overhead. Providers must employ either or both of: (ii) Negative Adjustment Method for accumulated cost, or (iii) Fragmenting (componentizing): Administrative and General Method, to prevent improper allocation of overhead on the Medicare cost report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative Adjustment Method: identifies mechanics for entering negative amounts on accumulated cost or reconciliation columns to exclude costs from allocation. Fragmenting Method: requires subscript/componentization of administrative/general cost center into 2+ cost centers using accurate statistics and tracking/allocating overhead based on actual resource consumption. Requests to change cost finding methods require 90 days' written notice to contractor; contractor determination is binding and approved method must be used for the reporting period and subsequent periods unless changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition criteria for an approved medical residency program
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved medical residency program means, subject to §413.84 requirements, a program that: (i) is approved by one of the national organizations listed in §415.152; (ii) may count towards certification of the participant in a specialty or subspecialty listed in specified directories (AMA Directory or ABMS Handbook); or (iii) is approved by ACGME, or other organization designated by the Secretary, as a fellowship program in geriatric medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the bases by which residency programs are recognized as 'approved' for direct GME payment purposes; cross-references other regulatory listings and accreditation.

rubrics_metrics.name: New medical residency training program composition requirement (90% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: For programs started on or after October 1, 2026, at least 90 percent of the individual residents that participate in the program during the 5-year cap building period must not have previous experience training in another program in the same specialty, subject to certain exclusions and exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes certain categories from the count (e.g., first-year residents who entered via NRMP or binding match programs, 'displaced residents'), and exempts programs accredited for 16 or fewer positions from the 90% requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition against unlawful discrimination (new §413.84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Addition of §413.84: Prohibition against unlawful discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section heading indicates CMS is establishing or codifying a prohibition on unlawful discrimination in the cost reimbursement/GME context; text of the provision is added as a new regulatory requirement (content not shown in this chunk).
